title: Sharp mapping complexes of marked interval path pullbacks
statement:
Use quasicategories, spaces and coherent functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the marked cartesian simplicial model, internal Hom and sharp mapping complexes of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Let $C,X,Y,Q$ be small quasicategories, let $f:X	o C$ and $g:Y	o C$ be arbitrary functors, and put $W=(C^
atural)^{(\Delta^1)^\sharp}$. Suppose $W	o C^
atural	imes C^
atural$ is a model fibration. Form the strict pullback of marked simplicial sets
$$H=(X^
atural	imes Y^
atural)	imes_{C^
atural	imes C^
atural}W.$$
Then $H$ is fibrant, so $H=R^
atural$ for its underlying quasicategory $R$. There is an isomorphism of Kan complexes
$$\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(Q^
atural,H)\cong\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(Q^
atural,X^
atural)	imes_{\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(Q^
atural,C^
atural),\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(Q^
atural,C^
atural))	imes_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(Q^
atural,C^
atural)}\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}(Q^
atural,Y^
atural).$$
This isomorphism preserves the projections and the specified interval path. It is natural in $Q$ and in strictly commuting maps of the cospans, and remains valid on enlarging the input universe. In particular it identifies the displayed mapping complex with the path-space homotopy pullback of the other three mapping Kan complexes.

source.place: HTT Section 3.1.3 internal marked Hom and sharp mapping complex, Corollary 3.1.4.4, and Remark A.2.4.5. Agent-formulated preservation-of-pullback/cotensor computation from returned Step 7; source read online on 2026-10-17. No Stacks tag supplies this marked formula.

proof.text:
Write $A=Q^
atural$, $B=X^
atural	imes Y^
atural$, $D=C^
atural	imes C^
atural$, and let $p:W	o D$ be endpoint evaluation. By the cited fibrant-object characterization, $X^
atural$ and $Y^
atural$ have the right lifting property against every trivial cofibration. A map from its domain into $B$ therefore extends by extending the two coordinates separately; hence $B$ is fibrant. To extend a marked map $u:S	o H$ across a trivial cofibration $i:S\hookrightarrow T$, first extend its $B$ coordinate to $b:T	o B$. The $W$ coordinate of $u$ and the map $T\xrightarrow{b}B	o D$ now form a lifting square against $p$. The assumed fibration $p$ supplies $w:T	o W$ over this map. The compatible pair $(b,w)$ gives the required extension $T	o H$. Thus $H$ is fibrant. The same characterization says its underlying simplicial set $R$ is a quasicategory and its marked edges are exactly the equivalences: $H=R^
atural$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.4.1; elementary coordinate lifting using the stated model structure.

proof.text:
The marked-model theorem supplies the Kan enrichment on fibrant objects. Apply it to the fibrant source $A=Q^
atural$ and to each of $H=R^
atural$, $X^
atural$, $Y^
atural$, and $C^
atural$. Consequently $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(A,H)$ and the three mapping complexes on the right of the asserted formula are Kan complexes. All these objects belong to the input universe. This uses the Kan-enrichment assertion of the cited statement, not merely its definition of marked maps.

source.place: Remark 3.1.3.1 and Corollary 3.1.4.4, applied over a point.

proof.text:
Put $I=\Delta^1$ and $M=\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(A,C^\natural)$. In simplicial degree $n$, internal-Hom adjunction, permutation of product factors, and the tensor/enrichment adjunction give the bijections
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(A,W)_n
&=\operatorname{Hom}_+(A\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,(C^\natural)^{I^\sharp})\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_+(A\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\times I^\sharp,C^\natural)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_+(A\times(\Delta^n\times I)^\sharp,C^\natural)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(\Delta^n\times I,M)
=\operatorname{Fun}(I,M)_n.
\end{aligned}$$
Here $\operatorname{Hom}_+$ denotes marked maps. The middle equality holds because an edge in either product is marked precisely when its $A$ coordinate is marked; both simplex coordinates are fully marked. The last adjunction is the defining tensor adjunction for the enrichment in the cited node, with tensor $A\otimes K=A\times K^\sharp$. Both currying operations have their evaluation operations as inverse. Precomposition by $\Delta(\alpha)\times I$ commutes with these bijections, so they give an isomorphism of simplicial sets. Restricting $I$ to either endpoint commutes with evaluation: the map induced by $W\to C^\natural$ becomes $\operatorname{ev}_e:\operatorname{Fun}(I,M)\to M$ for $e=0,1$.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, internal Hom and sharp mapping properties preceding Remark 3.1.3.1; Corollary 3.1.4.4 for the tensor convention.

proof.text: In degree $n$, the strict marked pullback defining $H$ says a marked map $A\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to H$ is uniquely a triple $(x,y,w)$ of marked maps into $X^\natural,Y^\natural,W$ with $f\circ x=\operatorname{ev}_0\circ w$ and $g\circ y=\operatorname{ev}_1\circ w$. Indeed its underlying map is the coordinatewise pullback map; it is marked because each projection is marked, and the pullback marking consists exactly of edges marked in every coordinate. Replace $w$ by its curried path $\gamma:\Delta^n\times I\to M$ from step 3. The two equations become $f_*x=\operatorname{ev}_0\gamma$ and $g_*y=\operatorname{ev}_1\gamma$. This is exactly an $n$-simplex of the displayed right-hand side. Uncurrying $\gamma$ and applying the pullback universal property gives the inverse bijection. Restrictions act on $x,y,w$ by the same precomposition, so these inverse bijections commute with all faces and degeneracies. They therefore give the asserted simplicial isomorphism, leaving $x,y$ and the specified interval path unchanged.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, sharp mapping definition; degreewise universal property of the marked pullback, written out.

proof.text:
For a functor $q:Q'	o Q$, precomposition sends the triple of step 4 to $(x\circ(q^
atural	imes\mathrm{id}),y\circ(q^
atural	imes\mathrm{id}),w\circ(q^
atural	imes\mathrm{id}))$. Its curried path is obtained by applying $q^*$ to $\gamma$ at every interval simplex. Thus the isomorphism commutes with restriction in $Q$. For a strictly commuting map of cospans given by $a:X	o X'$, $b:Y	o Y'$, $c:C	o C'$ with $cf=f'a$ and $cg=g'b$, postcomposition takes the uncurried triple to $(a\circ x,b\circ y,c\circ\widetilde\gamma)$, where $\widetilde\gamma$ is the marked map into $C^
atural$ adjoint to $w$. Currying the last coordinate gives $c_*\gamma$, so both routes around the naturality square send $(x,y,\gamma)$ to $(a_*x,b_*y,c_*\gamma)$. These formulas hold in every degree and also for the inverse bijections; they prove the two stated naturalities.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, naturality of the defining internal-Hom and tensor adjunctions; explicit coordinate formulas.

proof.text: In a larger input universe the same marked products, pullback tuples, marked maps and currying bijections are obtained on the original small objects, with the canonical universe lifts. The marked-model statement supplies the unchanged fibrant-object assertion there. Thus steps 1-5 and their formulas remain valid. Finally set $U=\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(A,X^\natural)$ and $V=\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(A,Y^\natural)$, with maps $f_*:U\to M$ and $g_*:V\to M$. The displayed right side is exactly the path-space model $U\times_{M,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,M)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,M}V$ meant by the path-space homotopy pullback in the statement. Step 4 identifies it by an isomorphism, and step 2 makes it a Kan complex. No fibration assumption on $f$ or $g$ was used: the only relative lift was against the stipulated endpoint fibration $p$.

source.place: Section 3.1.3 constructions relative to the input universe; path-space convention of the item (cf. Remark A.2.4.5).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NR-542f99226 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and all six steps in full, the full statements of both cited nodes (lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model, which is in this item's unit, and def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones), the parent's steps 7-9 and lem-coef-infinity-equivalence-arrow-path-object (it supplies the endpoint-fibration hypothesis, with the same W), the unit record, and blueprint prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint paragraph 2. HTT 3.1.3 and Cor 3.1.4.4 are not archived, so I could not read them at the cited place. The worker recorded WANTED and set proof_origin to agent; no step depends on HTT beyond what the cited marked-model statement says. Step 1: B is fibrant coordinatewise, the lift uses only the hypothesized fibration p, and fibrant objects are exactly the C^natural, so H = R^natural. Step 2: the Kan property comes from the simplicial structure (pushout-product axiom, every object cofibrant) and the stated Kan enrichment; it is correctly marked non-elementary. Step 3: the internal-Hom property, then (Delta^n)^sharp x I^sharp = (Delta^n x I)^sharp from the product-marking rule, then the tensor adjunction with tensor A x K^sharp, give Fun(I,M). Step 4: the degreewise marked pullback plus currying turns the endpoint equations into f_*x = ev_0 gamma and g_*y = ev_1 gamma, with uncurrying as inverse. Step 5: naturality in Q and in strictly commuting cospan maps is direct pre- and postcomposition. Step 6: universe stability holds, and 'path-space homotopy pullback' is literally the displayed model (def-cbc convention). Edge cases checked: Q empty gives a point on both sides; C empty or disjoint discrete images give empty on both sides; C a point gives the product mapping complex; degree 0 checked. No new nodes and no duplicate in the DAG (grep of Map^sharp/ev_0 and homotopy-pullback nodes). The statement is unchanged and not weakened, and no SGA source is used. No tool_uses and no fixes.
